## 4. Key Developments & Themes This Week

### 🧪 Varying Higgs VEV Opens New BSM-BBN Parameter Space
The 2609.18168 paper (accepted PRD) demonstrates that a modest 0.2–1.58% shift in the Higgs VEV during BBN can simultaneously address the cosmic lithium problem and accommodate the new EMPRESS He-4 measurement. This is a concrete example of how fundamental constants measured at accelerators connect to primordial nucleosynthesis — exactly the quarks-to-cosmos bridge. The requirement for non-standard cosmological evolution between BBN and recombination opens a new phenomenological window.

### 📊 Neutrino Mass Ordering Now "Decisive" — and Robust
Two complementary results this period cement the normal hierarchy:
1. **2606.18987**: Bayes factor K > 460 (NH vs IH) from DESI DR2 + Planck, robust across all prior constructions tested.
2. **2609.15970**: The Σm_ν bound is robust to non-standard thermal histories — even if massive BSM particles injected photons/DR after BBN, the bound shifts by < 0.004 eV.

This has profound implications: the effective Majorana mass is pushed to ~3.3 meV, well below the sensitivity of upcoming 0νββ experiments designed for the inverted-ordering regime.

### 🔧 Modified Gravity Gets One-Loop EFTofLSS Precision
The PyBird-MG release (2607.26945) is the most significant new tool for modified gravity analysis. It enables one-loop perturbation theory predictions for Horndeski gravity — previously only available for GR — and already delivers new constraints using BOSS + DESI DR2. Combined with ℋ-EFTCAMB (2603.01662), the community now has a complete CMB + LSS pipeline for arbitrary Horndeski models. This is directly relevant to our f(R) and modified gravity emulator program.

### 🤖 Domain-Specific AI Agents Converge on Verification-First Architecture
Three independent groups (FUSION for nuclear physics, ARC for theoretical physics, ScienceIDE for general scientific code) converge on the same design: domain-specific skills with built-in verification/benchmarks, deterministic computation delegated to specialized code, and LLMs restricted to planning/routing. This validates our Q2C MCP server architecture philosophy.
